display.title: Episode 4: The Return of Little Tzip Tzip
display.summary_short: A happy march, two young studio guests, and the story of Tzip Tzip the little bird, who smells something bad everywhere she flies until her mother finds the dirt on her own nose.
display.summary_long: Uncle Yossi begins by teaching that it is a mitzvah to be happy, "serve Hashem with joy", and everyone gets up to clap and march. Two young members of the Tzivos Hashem club visit the studio and say what they love about the show, and listeners say the Shema together. Story time is "The Return of Little Tzip Tzip": a baby bird leaves the nest for the first time and flies east, west, north and south, but comes straight home each time because everywhere smells bad. Her mother laughs and wipes away a speck of dirt on the tip of Tzip Tzip's own nose. Uncle Yossi draws the lesson: to love a fellow Jew, look at others with a good eye; the Baal Shem Tov taught that a fault we see in someone else is like a mirror, and the Sages say to correct ourselves first. After the sponsor, he explains that the Torah unites the Jewish people, and invites children and their whole families to get a letter in the new children's Sefer Torah.
display.lesson: Look at others with a good eye; a fault we see everywhere may really be our own, so correct yourself first.

sources_cited.note: 'Ivdu es Hashem b'simcha', cited as said by King David.
The Baal Shem Tov: a fault you see in another is like looking in a mirror.
'Kashet atzmecha techilah': first correct yourself, then correct others.
'Mitzvah goreres mitzvah', cited as a saying of the Sages.
